examples.en: Do you have a plan in mind for solving this problem?

examples.ko: 김 팀장님은 이미 나름의 복안을 갖고 계세요.
examples.en: Team Leader Kim already has a plan of his own in mind.
I can't tell you my plan yet.

examples.ko: 정부는 새 정책에 대한 복안을 발표했어요.
examples.en: The government announced its plan for the new policy.

examples.ko: 아무 복안 없이 시작하면 나중에 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you start without any plan in mind, it gets hard later.

examples.ko: 그 일은 복안대로 잘 진행되고 있어요.
examples.en: That work is going well, just as planned.

explain: '복안이 있다/없다'처럼 쓰는 일이 많고, 아직 밝히지 않은 속마음의 계획이라는 느낌이 있어요. 그냥 '계획'보다 격식 있어서 뉴스나 회의에서 자주 들려요. 친구끼리는 '생각이 있어' 정도로 말해요.

phrases.en: I have a plan of my own, too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속으로 생각해 둔 계획이 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means one has a plan in mind.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a plan in mind

phrases.en: I'm worried because I don't have a good plan yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대로 마땅한 계획이 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when, on the contrary, there is no suitable plan.

phrases.en: Please work out a plan before the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획을 미리 준비한다는 뜻으로 격식 있게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to say preparing a plan in advance.

explain_en: A plan one has thought through but not yet announced. It is mostly used as '복안이 있다/없다' and feels like a plan one keeps to oneself and hasn't revealed yet. It is more formal than '계획' and is heard in news and meetings. Among friends people would just say something like '생각이 있어'.

examples.en: The sunlight was strong, so I put on tinted glasses.
It's hard to walk along the beach without tinted glasses.

examples.ko: 이 색안경이 얼굴에 정말 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: These tinted glasses really suit your face.
I left my tinted glasses in the car when I got out.
The glare was bright, so I wore tinted glasses while driving.

examples.ko: 가게에서 마음에 드는 색안경을 하나 골랐어요.
examples.en: I picked out a pair of tinted glasses I liked at the store.

explain: 눈을 보호하려고 쓰는 짙은 색 안경이에요. 일상에서는 '선글라스'라고도 하는데, '색안경'은 편견을 가진 시선을 말할 때도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Don't look at someone with prejudice just because they're a foreigner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선입견이나 편견을 가지고 어떤 사람이나 일을 바라본다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means looking at a person or matter with preconceptions or bias.
phrases.en_equiv: view through tinted glasses; look with a biased eye

explain_en: It is dark-tinted glasses worn to protect the eyes. In daily talk people also say '선글라스', but '색안경' is the word often used for a prejudiced way of looking at someone.

en: to deliberate; to contemplate; to consider

examples.en: I deliberated for a long time about whether to move.
It's an important decision, so please think it over carefully.

examples.ko: 그는 숙고한 끝에 회사를 떠나기로 했어요.
examples.en: After careful consideration, he decided to leave the company.

examples.ko: 숙고하지 않고 계약서에 서명하면 나중에 후회해요.
examples.en: If you sign a contract without thinking it through, you'll regret it later.
I'll weigh the various opinions and come to a conclusion.
The teacher thought for a long while and then spoke.

explain: '생각하다'보다 신중하고 오래 따져 본다는 느낌이에요. '고민하다'는 걱정하며 힘들어하는 느낌이 있지만 '숙고하다'는 차분히 따져 보는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '곰곰이 생각하다'라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 문제는 곰곰이 생각해 보고 대답할게요.
phrases.en: I'll think this problem over carefully and then answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숙고하다'와 뜻이 같고, 일상 대화에서는 이 말을 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 숙고하다, but this is much more common in everyday conversation.

phrases.example: 숙고 끝에 이 회사에 가기로 했어요.
phrases.en: After careful deliberation, I decided to go to this company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 따져 본 뒤에 결론을 말할 때 쓰는 말로, 글이나 격식 있는 자리에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to introduce a conclusion reached after long thought; suits writing and formal speech.

phrases.example: 숙고한 결과 지금은 이사하지 않기로 했어요.
phrases.en: As a result of careful consideration, I decided not to move for now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숙고하다'에 '-ㄴ 결과'를 붙여 따져 본 뒤에 나온 결정을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attaches '-ㄴ 결과' to explain a decision that came out of careful thought.
phrases.en_equiv: as a result of careful consideration

explain_en: One person thinks long and deeply before deciding. It means thinking carefully and for a long time, more than plain '생각하다'. '고민하다' carries a feeling of worry and struggle, while '숙고하다' is calm weighing of options. In daily talk people often say '곰곰이 생각하다'.

t90.ax: I deliberated for a long time about whether to move.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 살던 집이 아련히 떠올라요.
examples.en: The house I lived in as a child comes faintly to mind.
A bell could be heard faintly from far away.
There is one song I remember dimly.
The mountain looked hazy in the fog.
I vaguely and wistfully recall my first love's face.

examples.ko: 아련히 남아 있는 그날의 냄새가 그리워요.
examples.en: I miss the faint scent of that day that still lingers.

explain: 또렷하지 않게 멀고 희미한데, 그리운 마음이 함께 들어 있어요. '희미하게'는 단순히 흐린 것이고, '아련히'는 추억이나 소리에 감정이 담길 때 잘 어울려요. 형용사 '아련하다'는 '아련한 추억'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: An old song drifts in faintly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아련히'와 뜻이 같아요. 형용사 '아련하다'에 '-게'를 붙인 말로, 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 아련히; it is the adjective 아련하다 with -게, and the two can be swapped.

phrases.en: My hometown house is a faint, fond memory to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '아련한'은 추억이나 기억 앞에 자주 붙어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective 아련한 often goes before memories.

phrases.en: When I think of that time, my heart aches softly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그리움이 섞인 쓸쓸한 기분을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a wistful feeling mixed with longing.

explain_en: Literary; faint, nostalgic, hazy memory or distant sight (아련히 떠오르다) It means faint and far away, with a touch of longing mixed in. '희미하게' just means unclear, while '아련히' suits memories and sounds that carry emotion. The adjective '아련하다' is used as in '아련한 추억'.

t90.ax: There is one song I remember dimly.

en: to feel relieved; to breathe easy

examples.en: I felt relieved after seeing the exam result.
Everyone was relieved to hear the child was safe.

examples.ko: 길을 찾은 뒤에야 안도할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: I could only feel relieved after finding the way.
My parents felt relieved at the news that I had arrived.
When the rain stopped, people had relieved looks.
He took a deep breath, feeling relieved.

explain: '다행이다'는 일이 잘 풀려서 좋다는 마음이고, '안도하다'는 걱정하던 일이 끝나서 마음이 놓이는 모습을 말해요. 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 쓰고, 말할 때는 '마음이 놓이다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 합격 소식을 듣고 안도의 한숨을 쉬었어요.
phrases.en: breathe a sigh of relief
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정이 끝났을 때 숨을 길게 내쉬는 모습으로 말해요. 실제 한숨이 아니어도 마음이 놓였다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the long breath you let out when a worry ends. It can be used even without an actual sigh, to mean you feel relieved.

explain_en: Literary, formal; relief after danger or tension passes. '다행이다' is feeling glad that things turned out well; '안도하다' describes the moment your mind settles because a worry is over. It is common in writing and news; in speech '마음이 놓이다' is more natural.

t90.ax: He took a deep breath, feeling relieved.

en: complacency; attitude of taking the easy way

examples.en: If a company falls into complacency, it's hard for it to grow.
The boss is very worried about the employees' complacency.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 안일주의 때문에 큰 실수를 했어요.
examples.en: That team made a big mistake because of its take-it-easy attitude.

examples.ko: 이제 안일주의를 버리고 새로운 방법을 찾아봐요.
examples.en: Let's drop the complacency and look for a new method.

examples.ko: 공무원 사회의 안일주의를 비판하는 기사를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read an article criticizing the complacency in the civil service.
We have to be careful not to let complacency spread.

explain: 어렵거나 힘든 일은 피하고 편한 쪽만 택하는 태도를 비판할 때 써요. '무사안일주의'라고도 하고, 회의나 뉴스처럼 조금 딱딱한 자리에서 나와요. 보통 '안일주의에 빠지다', '안일주의를 버리다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 성공한 뒤에 안일주의에 빠지는 사람이 많아요.
phrases.en: Many people fall into complacency after they succeed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '안일주의'와 가장 자주 쓰는 표현으로, 편한 쪽에만 익숙해진 상태를 비판해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase with 안일주의; it criticizes getting used to taking the easy way.

phrases.example: 우리는 안일주의를 버리고 새롭게 시작해야 해요.
phrases.en: We have to give up our complacency and start anew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 태도를 바꾸자고 말할 때 쓰며, 회의나 연설에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when urging a change of attitude, often heard in meetings and speeches.

phrases.en: We couldn't prevent the accident because of a play-it-safe, do-nothing attitude.
phrases.nuance_ko: '안일주의'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 '탈 없이 지내려는' 태도가 더 분명한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning, but it more clearly stresses an attitude of avoiding any trouble.

explain_en: The doctrine or habit of choosing ease, more like an ism. It is used to criticize an attitude of avoiding hard things and choosing only what is easy. It is also said as '무사안일주의' and appears in somewhat formal settings like meetings and the news. Typical patterns are '안일주의에 빠지다' and '안일주의를 버리다'.

examples.en: Don't guess; find out exactly.

examples.ko: 사람이 백 명쯤 온 것 같다고 어림짐작했어요.
examples.en: I roughly estimated that about a hundred people had come.
My rough guess wasn't far off.

examples.ko: 거리를 어림짐작해서 걸음 수를 세어 봤어요.
examples.en: I estimated the distance and counted my steps.
It's risky to decide things based only on guesswork.
Rough guesses often miss the mark.

explain: 정확한 계산이나 확인 없이 대충 헤아려 맞히는 것에 써요. '어림짐작으로', '어림짐작하다'처럼 쓰고, 정확하지 않다는 느낌이 있어서 중요한 결정에는 안 좋은 방법으로 말해요.

phrases.en: It'll take about an hour, roughly speaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대충 헤아려서 말할 때 문장 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed at the start of a sentence when giving a rough estimate.

phrases.en: My rough guess turned out to be right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대충 한 짐작이 결과적으로 맞았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a casual guess turned out to be correct.

phrases.en: Please don't speak based on a rough guess.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어림짐작하다와 비슷하지만 일상에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 어림짐작하다 but easier and more common in daily speech.

explain_en: Casual rough guess, such as a number, without exact checking. It is used for guessing roughly without exact calculation or checking. It appears as '어림짐작으로' or '어림짐작하다', and carries a sense of imprecision, so it is often mentioned as a poor basis for important decisions.

en: to be questionable; to be doubtful; to be dubious

examples.en: His explanation is a little questionable.
The results came out so fast that I was doubtful.
If anything seems doubtful, ask right away.
I got a strange and dubious phone call.

examples.ko: 뉴스 내용이 의문스러워서 다른 곳도 찾아봤어요.
examples.en: The news content seemed dubious, so I checked other sources too.

examples.ko: 의문스러울 때는 자료를 한 번 더 확인해요.
examples.en: When in doubt, I check the data once more.

explain: '이상하다'는 보통과 다르다는 느낌이고, '의문스럽다'는 믿기 어렵거나 이유를 잘 모르겠다는 느낌이에요. 말할 때는 '수상하다', '이상하다'를 더 많이 써요. 활용은 '의문스러워요', '의문스러운'처럼 ㅂ이 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: There is something doubtful in this contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의문스러운'은 명사 앞에서 믿기 어려운 부분을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, '의문스러운' points to a part that is hard to believe.

phrases.en: What that person said seems a bit doubtful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 지금의 느낌을 말하는 가장 기본적인 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic polite form for stating how it seems now.

phrases.example: 그 가게는 가격이 너무 싸서 수상해요.
phrases.en: That shop's prices are so low that it seems suspicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '의문스럽다'보다 '수상하다'가 더 자주 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, '수상하다' is used more often than '의문스럽다'.

explain_en: Something's truth or quality raises a question. 이상하다 means different from normal; 의문스럽다 means hard to believe or unclear why. In speech 수상하다 and 이상하다 are used more. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective: 의문스러워요, 의문스러운.

examples.en: After I took the medicine, my cough calmed down.
Let's talk again once you've calmed down.
The protest settled down as night came.
We started the meeting in a calmer atmosphere.
Prices seem likely to settle soon.
When the child is held, the crying settles.

explain: '진정하다'는 내가 마음을 가라앉히는 것이고, '진정되다'는 흥분·통증·소란이 저절로 가라앉는 것이에요. '진정하세요'는 '진정하다'의 명령이라 흥분한 사람에게 해요. '진정되다'는 사람에게 명령하지 않아요.

phrases.en: After taking medicine, my fever went down.
phrases.nuance_ko: '진정되다'보다 쉬운 말이고 통증·감정에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word, used for pain and feelings.

phrases.en: Please calm down a little and speak slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 직접 마음을 가라앉히는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, calming yourself down.

phrases.en: My excitement hasn't calmed down yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 가라앉지 않은 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state that has not yet settled.

explain_en: Passive — a feeling or situation settles by itself. '진정하다' is you calming yourself; '진정되다' is excitement, pain or commotion subsiding on its own. '진정하세요' (calm down!) comes from '진정하다'; you don't give commands with '진정되다'.

t90.ax: Prices seem likely to settle soon.

examples.ko: 추리 소설을 읽으면 시간이 빨리 가요.
examples.en: Time flies when I read a mystery novel.
The detective began reasoning from a small clue.
His deduction was accurate, so everyone was surprised.

examples.ko: 추리의 재미는 범인을 맞히는 데 있어요.
examples.en: The fun of a mystery is in guessing the culprit.
There were few clues, so the deduction had limits.
This game needs deduction and a way with words.

explain: '추리 소설', '추리 영화'처럼 이야기 장르 이름으로 가장 자주 나와요. '추론'은 논리나 공부에서 쓰는 말이고, '추리'는 사건과 범인처럼 단서를 모아 짐작할 때 어울려요. 단서 없이 막연히 하는 것은 '짐작'이에요.

phrases.en: I played a mystery deduction game with friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단서를 모아 범인을 찾는 놀이를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A game where you gather clues to find the culprit.

phrases.en: I tried to deduce from a small clue.
phrases.nuance_ko: '추리하다'와 같은 뜻이지만 '를 하다' 형태로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same as 추리하다 but in the '를 하다' form.

phrases.en: That friend is good at deduction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단서로 생각해 내는 능력을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ability to figure things out from clues.

explain_en: Most often seen as a story genre, as in '추리 소설' and '추리 영화'. '추론' is used in logic and academics, while 추리 fits gathering clues about a case or culprit. Guessing with no clues is '짐작'.

t90.ax: Time flies when I read a mystery novel.

en: to be pathetic; to be pitiable; to be deplorable

examples.en: I feel pathetic when I put off my homework.

examples.ko: 같은 실수를 또 한 제가 한심스러웠어요.
examples.en: I felt pathetic for making the same mistake again.
That kind of behavior looks truly pitiful.
Please stop the pathetic excuses.
My friend looked at me with a look that said I was pathetic.

examples.ko: 아무것도 안 하고 하루를 보낸 게 한심스럽게 느껴져요.
examples.en: Spending the day doing nothing feels pathetic.

explain: '한심하다'와 거의 같아요. 남에게 직접 말하면 모욕이 되니 조심하세요. 자기 자신에게 쓰면 스스로를 탓하는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I look pathetic when I oversleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보이는 모습이 한심하게 느껴질 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used when something looks pathetic.

phrases.en: I felt pathetic about myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로의 마음을 말할 때 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural way to describe your own feelings.

phrases.en: I'm pathetic for making the same mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한심스럽다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 조금 더 짧고 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning, a bit shorter and more common.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '한심하다'. Saying it directly to someone is insulting, so be careful. Used about yourself, it feels like blaming yourself.

examples.en: The revised edition of the dictionary came out this month.
Many new words were added in the revised edition.
The teacher told us to use the revised textbook.
The revised edition and the first edition have different page counts.

examples.ko: 저자가 십 년 만에 개정판을 냈어요.
examples.en: The author put out a revised edition after ten years.

examples.ko: 이 책은 두 번째 개정판이라서 내용이 더 정확해요.
examples.en: This is the second revised edition, so the content is more accurate.

explain: 책의 판은 '초판', '개정판', '증보판'처럼 불러요. 개정판은 틀린 곳을 고치거나 새 내용을 넣었을 때, 증보판은 내용을 늘렸을 때 많이 써요. 서점에서는 '개정판 출간'이라고 광고해요.

phrases.en: A revised edition of that book came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 판이 출간됐다는 소식을 전할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for announcing a new edition.

phrases.en: I bought the revised edition instead of the old book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛 판과 비교해서 새 판을 고를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when choosing the new edition over the old one.

phrases.example: 서점에 개정판 출간 광고가 붙어 있어요.
phrases.en: There is an ad for a revised edition release at the bookstore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고나 기사 제목처럼 짧게 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short, headline-style phrase seen in ads and news.

explain_en: Updated published edition of a book (선생님이 추천해 주신 책의 개정판이 이번 달에 나왔어요.) Book editions are called things like '초판', '개정판', and '증보판'. A 개정판 corrects mistakes or adds new content, while a 증보판 expands it. Bookstores advertise a new one as '개정판 출간'.

examples.en: I went to the baseball park at the weekend.

examples.ko: 새 구장이 다음 달에 문을 열어요.
examples.en: The new ballpark opens next month.
We agreed to meet in front of the stadium.
The grass at this ballpark is really beautiful.

examples.ko: 우리 동네에는 작은 축구 구장이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small football ground in our neighbourhood.

examples.ko: 구장 안에서 먹는 치킨이 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: Chicken eaten inside the ballpark tastes best.

explain: 구장은 야구나 축구처럼 공으로 하는 경기를 하는 곳이에요. 한국에서는 특히 야구장을 말할 때 많이 써서 '잠실 구장'처럼 불러요. 축구는 '축구장'이나 '경기장'이라고도 하고, 아주 큰 경기장은 '스타디움'이라고 하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I ate chicken at the baseball stadium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구 구장과 같은 말이고, 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same as 야구 구장 but used more often in speech.

phrases.en: There are many people at the stadium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모든 운동 경기를 하는 곳을 넓게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word for any place where sports matches are held.

phrases.example: 잠실 구장은 지하철로 갈 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can get to Jamsil Stadium by subway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지역 이름을 앞에 붙여 구장을 구별해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A place name before 구장 tells which ballpark.

explain_en: Gujang is a place where ball games such as baseball or football are played. In Korea it is used especially for baseball parks, as in 잠실 구장. Football grounds are also called 축구장 or 경기장, and very large ones 스타디움.
